subject: business_studies
chapter_title: Where Do Companies Do Their Business? In the Markets or in the Society?

concepts.title: Meaning and Nature of Marketing
concepts.definition: Marketing is the whole set of activities -- from sensing what buyers want before anything is produced to service after the sale -- through which goods and services flow from maker to user in exchange for value; it is a social process of creating offers and trading them freely.
concepts.key_idea: Selling is only one spoke; the wheel starts before production and keeps turning after the product is sold.
question_patterns: explain the meaning and nature of marketing
why is marketing more than just selling goods
describe marketing as a social process of exchange
when does marketing begin and end for a product
what activities together make up marketing
how does marketing create a market offering for buyers

solution_steps.explain: marketing covers product designing, packaging, branding, pricing, promotion and distribution -- not just the sale moment
need identification and product development happen before production; after-sale service happens after the sale
people obtain what they need and want by creating offerings and freely exchanging things of value with others

concepts.title: Marketing Management Philosophies
concepts.definition: Firms have progressed through five philosophies: the production concept chases availability and affordability, the product concept chases quality, the selling concept pushes whatever is made, the marketing concept starts from customer needs, and the societal marketing concept adds the long-run welfare of society to customer satisfaction and profit.
concepts.formula: evolution_of_philosophies = production_concept + product_concept + selling_concept + marketing_concept + societal_marketing_concept
concepts.key_idea: Each step of the ladder widens the firm's attention -- from the factory, to the product, to the hard sell, to the customer, and finally to society.
question_patterns: explain the five marketing management philosophies
distinguish the product concept from the production concept
what does the societal marketing concept add to the marketing concept
how does the selling concept differ from the marketing concept
which philosophy focuses on availability and affordability
state the assumption behind the selling concept of marketing

solution_steps.explain: production concept stresses cheap mass availability, product concept stresses quality and features, selling concept stresses aggressive promotion of existing stock
identifying market needs and delivering satisfaction better than competitors becomes the route to profit
customer wants are met only as far as society's long-run well-being -- health, environment, fair dealing -- is not harmed

concepts.title: Marketing versus Selling
concepts.definition: Selling transfers ownership of a finished product for money, starting after production and ending with the sale; marketing is the far wider canvas that starts long before the product exists, keeps the customer's need at the centre, and profits through satisfaction and repeat business.
concepts.key_idea: Selling stares at the product and the day's turnover; marketing stares at the customer and the whole relationship.
question_patterns: distinguish between marketing and selling
how does the scope of marketing exceed that of selling
where does selling start and end compared with marketing
which view is customer oriented and which product oriented
compare the profit emphasis of marketing and selling
is selling a part of marketing or the other way round

solution_steps.explain: selling concentrates on the product and converting it into cash; marketing concentrates on customer needs and total satisfaction
selling begins after production; marketing begins before production with need identification and continues after the sale
selling aims at profit through sales volume; marketing aims at profit through customer satisfaction that brings repeat sales

concepts.title: Functions of Marketing
concepts.definition: Marketing performs a chain of jobs: collecting and analysing market information, planning, designing and developing the product, standardising and grading, packaging and labelling, branding, fixing prices, promoting, distributing physically, transporting, warehousing and serving customers after the sale.
concepts.formula: functions_of_marketing = market_information + product_design + standardisation_and_grading + packaging_and_labelling + branding + pricing + promotion + physical_distribution + customer_support
concepts.key_idea: Every function either shapes the offer, informs the buyer, or moves and protects the goods on the way to the customer.
question_patterns: list the important functions of marketing
explain standardisation and grading as marketing functions
what marketing work happens before production begins
how does transportation and warehousing serve marketing
describe the role of customer support services in marketing
name the function behind fixing a market share target and action programme

solution_steps.action: group the gathering and shaping jobs
solution_steps.explain: market information, marketing planning and product designing and development decide what will be offered
standardisation and grading, packaging and labelling, and branding give the product identity and assurance
pricing, promotion, transportation, warehousing, physical distribution and customer support carry the offer to buyers and keep them satisfied

concepts.title: Marketing Mix and its Elements
concepts.definition: The marketing mix is the set of controllable tools a firm blends to answer its market: product (what is offered), price (what is charged), place (how it reaches buyers) and promotion (how buyers are told and persuaded), with each element carrying its own sub-decisions.
concepts.key_idea: The mix must hang together -- a premium product with poor distribution or no promotion fails -- so the elements are chosen as one package.
question_patterns: what is the marketing mix and name its elements
explain the four P's of marketing with examples
why must the elements of the mix be coordinated
what decisions fall under the price element of the mix
how does the place element deliver the product to buyers
describe the promotion element of the marketing mix

solution_steps.explain: product covers brand, package, label and the bundle of utilities the buyer receives

solution_steps.action: fix the money and the route
solution_steps.explain: price covers list price, margins and discounts; place covers channels, transport and inventory
promotion blends advertising, personal selling, sales promotion and publicity, and all four Ps are adjusted together for the target market

concepts.title: Classification of Products
concepts.definition: Products split into consumer products bought for personal use and industrial products used as inputs; consumer goods are further sorted by shopping effort into convenience, shopping and speciality products, and by durability into non-durable, durable and services.
concepts.key_idea: The buyer's effort and the product's life decide the class, and the class decides the marketing treatment.
question_patterns: how are products classified on the basis of durability
distinguish convenience products from shopping products
what makes a product a speciality product
how do industrial products differ from consumer products
classify goods into consumer and industrial categories
give instances of non-durable goods and services

solution_steps.explain: bought for final consumption means consumer product; bought as input for other products means industrial product
convenience goods need almost no effort, shopping goods are compared on quality and price, speciality goods are hunted for specifically
non-durables are consumed quickly, durables last many uses, and services are intangible performances

concepts.title: Branding and Brand Name
concepts.definition: Branding gives a product an identity that separates it from identical rival offerings: the brand is the overall identification, the brand name is the speakable part, the brand mark is the design, and a registered brand becomes a trademark; a good name is short, distinctive, adaptable and lasting.
concepts.key_idea: A brand turns a commodity into a promise, letting the firm charge differently and win repeat buyers.
concepts.textbook_ref: lebs202.txt Branding, Characteristics of Good Brand Name (lines 1454-1589)
question_patterns: what is branding and why do firms brand their products
distinguish brand, brand name, brand mark and trademark
state the qualities of a good brand name
how does branding help in product differentiation
what advantages does branding give to marketers
how does branding support differential pricing

solution_steps.explain: brand names the product in words, the brand mark is the symbol or design, and legal registration makes it a trademark
branding enables product differentiation, differential pricing, easier promotion and customer loyalty
a good name is short, easy to pronounce and remember, distinctive, adaptable to packaging and labelling, and capable of legal protection

concepts.title: Packaging and Labelling
concepts.definition: Packaging wraps the product at three levels -- primary wrapper, secondary carton and transport packaging -- protecting it, promoting it and easing use, while the label on the package identifies, describes, grades, promotes and legally warns through printed information.
concepts.key_idea: The package is the silent salesman on the shelf, and the label is the voice printed on it.
concepts.textbook_ref: lebs202.txt Packaging, Levels of Packaging, Labelling (lines 1590-1851)
question_patterns: explain the levels of packaging with instances
state the functions packaging performs for a product
what information does a label carry for the buyer
how does packaging act as a promotional tool
distinguish the primary and secondary package of a product
list the functions of labelling in marketing

solution_steps.explain: primary packaging holds the product itself, secondary protects it in handling, transportation packaging ships it in bulk
protection, easy identification, self-promotion through colour and design, convenience in use and compliance with law
identify the product, describe contents and use, grade the quality, promote through appeal and warn where hazardous

concepts.title: Factors Determining Price
concepts.definition: The price a firm settles on is pulled by several forces: the cost of the product setting the floor, the utility and demand of the buyer setting the ceiling, the extent of competition, government regulation of prices, the firm's own pricing objectives and the marketing methods in use.
concepts.key_idea: Cost says do not go below, demand says do not go above, and competition, law and objectives squeeze the band further.
question_patterns: what factors affect the determination of price of a product
how does cost set the floor and demand the ceiling of price
why does the extent of competition influence pricing
how can government regulation fix or cap prices
how do pricing objectives like market share leadership shape price
explain the role of utility and demand in fixing price

solution_steps.explain: total cost -- fixed plus variable -- is the lowest level at which the product can profitably be offered
the utility to the buyer and the price of rival goods cap what the market will bear
competition, government controls, the firm's objectives -- profit, share, survival -- and chosen marketing methods pin the final figure inside the band

concepts.title: Physical Distribution and its Components
concepts.definition: Physical distribution carries the product physically from the factory to the customer through four linked decisions: order processing, transportation, warehousing and inventory control, all aimed at the right goods arriving at the right place and time at least cost.
concepts.key_idea: Distribution decisions trade service level against cost -- more warehouses and faster transport please customers but eat margins.
question_patterns: what are the components of physical distribution
explain the role of transportation in physical distribution
why do firms hold inventories and warehouses
how does order processing start the distribution chain
what trade-off does the choice of number of channels involve
describe inventory control as a distribution decision

solution_steps.explain: order processing receives, bills and routes the order, setting the whole chain in motion
transportation decides the mode that balances speed and cost; warehousing stores goods near demand to bridge the time gap
inventory control decides how much to hold so that service stays high while carrying cost stays low

concepts.title: Promotion Mix and its Tools
concepts.definition: The promotion mix is the blend of four communication tools -- advertising, personal selling, sales promotion and publicity or public relations -- chosen together so that buyers learn about, trust and buy the product.
concepts.key_idea: Mass tools build reach and image; face-to-face tools build conviction; the right blend depends on the product and the market.
question_patterns: name the elements of the promotion mix
explain promotion as an element of the marketing mix
how do the four promotion tools differ from each other
which promotion tool reaches the largest audience
when would a firm rely on personal selling over advertising
what role does publicity play in the promotion mix

solution_steps.explain: advertising and publicity speak to many at once without a salesman; personal selling speaks to one buyer at a time
sales promotion supplies temporary incentives -- discounts, premiums, contests -- to speed up the buying decision
the mix depends on the product's complexity, the buyers' kind and the funds available

concepts.title: Advertising and Personal Selling
concepts.definition: Advertising is a paid, impersonal message from an identified sponsor reaching a mass audience at low cost per contact, while personal selling is an oral, face-to-face presentation that is flexible, gives instant feedback and closes the sale -- the two differ on reach, cost, feedback and flexibility.
concepts.key_idea: Advertising whispers to millions and cannot answer back; the salesperson speaks to one and can.
question_patterns: define advertising and state its features
what merits and objections surround advertising
distinguish between advertising and personal selling
why is advertising called an impersonal form of communication
what makes personal selling flexible as a promotion tool
is expenditure on advertising a social waste, discuss

solution_steps.explain: paid form, identified sponsor, impersonal and mass reach, unified message, low cost per contact
oral presentation, direct contact, flexible message, immediate feedback, high cost per contact
objections such as higher prices, undermining values and confusing buyers are answered by the information and scale economies advertising provides

concepts.title: Sales Promotion Techniques
concepts.definition: Sales promotion is the short-term incentive layer of promotion -- rebates, discounts, refunds, product combinations, quantity gifts, lucky draws, contests, sampling and zero-percent finance -- used to push buyers to act now and to back up advertising and selling.
concepts.key_idea: Where advertising persuades slowly, a time-limited offer makes the customer buy on the spot.
concepts.textbook_ref: lebs202.txt Sales Promotion, Commonly used activities (lines 2696-2836)
question_patterns: what is sales promotion and why is it undertaken
list the commonly used sales promotion techniques
how does a rebate differ from a discount as a promotion tool
which sales promotion tool suits the launch of a new product
state the merits and limitations of sales promotion
give instances of quantity gift and lucky draw offers

solution_steps.explain: rebates clear excess stock, discounts cut the list price, refunds return part of the price on proof of purchase

solution_steps.action: spot the gift and chance tools
solution_steps.explain: product combinations and quantity gifts add value; instant draws, lucky draws and contests add the excitement of winning

solution_steps.action: spot the trial and finance tools
solution_steps.explain: sampling lets buyers try free; usable benefits and zero-percent finance ease the purchase of durables

worked_examples.question_pattern: A colour TV marketer with a fifth of the market wants half the market in three years and lays down an action programme. Which marketing function is at work?

solution_template.explain: an objective for market share backed by an action programme points to planning
marketing planning is the function that sets objectives, strategies and programmes in writing

worked_examples.question_pattern: Classify salt, a television set and a tailor's stitching into the durability classes of products.

solution_template.explain: salt is used up quickly, the television serves for years, stitching is an intangible performance
salt is a non-durable good, the television a durable good, stitching a service
